issues.display_title: Issue #5: [Create Tour] Integrate Create Tour Real Estate
issues.main_description_html:
[Create Tour] Integrate Create Tour — Real Estate (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN create-tour flow (src/pages/create-tour) + listings/real-estate handling (src/pages/listings). See docs/analyze.md §2 (capabilities 2 & 6) and §3.3 — a project carries project_type and a listing flag, and real-estate tours capture address + listing attributes (attr).

Goal

Implement the "Create Tour" flow for the Real Estate tour type in the Flutter app: the user starts a new tour, selects/branches into the Real Estate type, fills the required real-estate metadata, and a project is persisted locally with the correct project_type and listing data.

Scope

  • Create Tour entry → choose Real Estate type.
  • Real-estate form: project/listing name, address (map/lat-lng), and listing attributes (attr).
  • Persist a projects row with project_type = real estate, listing = 1, address, and attr populated.
  • Navigate into the project (ready to add panoramas/levels) on success.
  • Validation for required fields; localized labels.

Out of Scope

  • Google Business create-tour flow (separate task).
  • Upload/publish to GoThru (separate task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Real Estate option available in the Create Tour flow.
  • Required real-estate fields validated before a project is created.
  • New project saved locally with correct project_type, listing = 1, address, and attr.
  • On success, user lands in the new project ready to add content.
  • Labels sourced from i18n; works offline (local persistence only).

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Create a Real Estate tour (happy path)

  1. Tap Create Tour → select Real Estate.
  2. Fill name, address, and required listing attributes.
  3. Submit.
  4. Expected: Project is created and opens; it appears in the project list flagged as a real-estate/listing tour.

TC-2 — Required-field validation

  1. Start a Real Estate tour and leave a required field empty.
  2. Submit.
  3. Expected: Inline validation message; project is NOT created until valid.

TC-3 — Address / location capture

  1. Set the address via map/lat-lng.
  2. Save and reopen the project.
  3. Expected: Address + coordinates persisted and shown correctly.

TC-4 — Offline creation

  1. Put device offline.
  2. Create a Real Estate tour.
  3. Expected: Project saves locally with no error; available after reopening the app.

TC-5 — Persisted type correctness

  1. Create a Real Estate tour, then inspect the project.
  2. Expected: project_type = real estate and listing flag set; data round-trips after app restart.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch app language and repeat creation.
  2. Expected: Form labels/validation translated; no raw i18n keys.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: generic (non-real-estate) tour creation still works.

Demo by Developer

QA Test Summary — Issue #5: Create Tour Real Estate

Verdict: Passed — no Real Estate address-field defect.

Current Acceptance Criteria

The developer description predates the confirmed product behaviour. The current
flow is intentionally split by tour type:

Tour type Required create input Address / map location
Real Estate Tour title only Not collected during creation
Google Business Business selected through the location picker Required before Continue is enabled

Accordingly, the previous QA failure for the missing Real Estate address,
coordinates, and listing-attribute form is invalid and has been superseded.
Google Business location capture remains outside this issue's scope.

QA Review

Check Evidence Result
Real Estate entry is available TourCategory.realEstate is selectable and opens CreateTourScreen. Pass
Real Estate title validation The Real Estate branch renders one Tour Name field; Continue is enabled only when its trimmed value is non-empty. Pass
No Real Estate address input The Real Estate branch intentionally has no location picker or address validation. Pass — expected behaviour
Google Business location separation Only the Google Business branch renders _LocationPickerCard; its Continue condition requires latitude and longitude. Pass — correctly separated from Real Estate
Local draft persistence and next navigation createDraft writes the project and default ground level transactionally, then calls openTourAfterCreate. Pass (source review)

White / Gray / Black Box Coverage

Method Scenario Expected Result
White box Inspect CreateTourScreen category branches Real Estate has title-only UI; Google Business owns location UI Pass
Gray box Trace Real Estate createDraft persistence Local project and default level are created before navigation Pass
Black box (static) Try to continue with an empty Real Estate title Continue remains unavailable Pass
Black box (static) Enter a Real Estate title without an address Continue is allowed Pass — intended behaviour

Test Execution Boundary

This update is based on fresh source review of the current Flutter flow. A
targeted local Flutter test command was started but did not complete within the
120-second execution window, so no new runtime-test count is claimed here. No
Android/iOS device run, screenshot, or video was required to resolve the
reported acceptance-criteria mismatch.

Final Conclusion

Issue #5 should not be reported as failing because it lacks an address form in
Real Estate creation. The title-only Real Estate flow matches the confirmed
product behaviour. Address selection must be tested under the separate Google
Business flow.

[Create Tour] Integrate Create Tour — Google Business (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN create-tour flow (src/pages/create-tour). A project's project_type distinguishes tour kinds (see docs/analyze.md §3.3). Google Business tours target Google Street View / Business Profile publishing, so the create flow captures the place/business location and the Google-specific tour type.

Goal

Implement the "Create Tour" flow for the Google Business tour type in the Flutter app: the user starts a new tour, selects the Google Business type, provides the place/business location, and a project is persisted locally with the correct project_type.

Scope

  • Create Tour entry → choose Google Business type.
  • Capture business/place name + location (map/lat-lng, address).
  • Persist a projects row with project_type = google business and address populated.
  • Navigate into the project (ready to add panoramas/levels) on success.
  • Validation for required fields; localized labels.

Out of Scope

  • Real Estate create-tour flow (separate task).
  • Actual Google/GoThru publishing (separate task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Google Business option available in the Create Tour flow.
  • Required fields (place name, location) validated before creation.
  • New project saved locally with correct project_type = google business and address.
  • On success, user lands in the new project ready to add content.
  • Labels sourced from i18n; works offline (local persistence only).

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Create a Google Business tour (happy path)

  1. Tap Create Tour → select Google Business.
  2. Enter business/place name and set location.
  3. Submit.
  4. Expected: Project is created and opens; appears in the project list as a Google Business tour.

TC-2 — Required-field validation

  1. Start a Google Business tour and leave a required field empty.
  2. Submit.
  3. Expected: Inline validation message; project is NOT created until valid.

TC-3 — Location capture

TC-4 — Offline creation

TC-6 — Type separation

  1. Create one Google Business and one Real Estate tour.

[Level] Integrate Default Level (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN multi-level support — the levels table groups panoramas into floors/levels, and panoramas default to level_id = 1 (see docs/analyze.md §2.4 and §3.3). When a tour is created it must have a usable default level so panoramas have somewhere to belong before the user adds more levels.

Goal

Ensure every newly created tour automatically gets a default level, and that panoramas added without an explicit level are assigned to it — replicating the RN behavior in the Flutter app on top of the new local DB layer.

Scope

  • On project creation, create a default levels row for the project (e.g. default name / position 0).
  • Assign new panoramas to the default level (level_id) when no level is chosen.
  • Default level appears in the level list/selector for the project.
  • Default level is not duplicated on subsequent opens of the same project.

Out of Scope

  • Full level management UI (add/rename/reorder/delete levels) — separate task.
  • Moving panoramas between levels — separate task.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Creating a tour produces exactly one default level for that project.
  • Panoramas added without a chosen level are linked to the default level.
  • Default level is visible/selectable in the project.
  • Reopening the project does not create duplicate default levels.
  • Behavior works offline (local DB only) and survives app restart.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Default level on tour creation

  1. Create a new tour (any type).
  2. Open the level list/selector.
  3. Expected: Exactly one default level exists for the project.

TC-2 — Panorama assigned to default level

  1. In a new tour, add a panorama without selecting a level.
  2. Expected: The panorama is grouped under the default level (correct level_id).

TC-3 — No duplicate default level

  1. Create a tour, close it, and reopen it several times.
  2. Expected: Still exactly one default level — no duplicates created on reopen.

TC-4 — Persistence after restart

  1. Create a tour, force-close and relaunch the app, reopen the project.
  2. Expected: Default level and its panoramas persist (local DB).

TC-5 — Offline behavior

  1. Put device offline, create a tour and add panoramas.
  2. Expected: Default level created and panoramas assigned with no network/errors.

TC-6 — Coexistence with manual levels

  1. Create a tour (default level present), then add a second level manually.
  2. Expected: Default level remains intact; the two levels are distinct and panoramas stay on their assigned level.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: existing projects (if any seed/migrated data) are not broken by default-level creation.

issues.display_title: Issue #9: [Tour Detail] Integrate Add Panorama from Phone
issues.main_description_html:
[Tour Detail] Integrate Add Panorama from Phone (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN imports equirectangular panoramas from the device gallery (expo-image-picker); see docs/analyze.md §2.1 and the panoramas data model in §3.3.

Goal

Implement, in Tour Detail, the "Add Panorama from Phone" flow: pick one or more 360° images from the device gallery, store them locally, and persist panoramas rows linked to the project.

Scope

  • Image picker (gallery) with photo permission handling.
  • Save selected image(s) to the app's Panorama folder (filesystem) and generate thumbnail/small variants.
  • Insert panoramas rows: panorama_original/thumbnail/small, width/height, filename, level_id (default level), project_id.
  • New panoramas appear in the Tour Detail list immediately.

Out of Scope

  • Camera 360 capture (separate task), connections/auto-link, upload to GoThru.

Acceptance Criteria

  • User can pick 360° image(s) from the gallery (with permission prompt handled).
  • Image(s) saved locally; thumbnail/small variants generated; dimensions stored.
  • panoramas row(s) created with correct project_id and default level_id.
  • Added panoramas render in Tour Detail without restart.
  • Works offline; labels via i18n.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Add a single panorama from gallery (happy path)

  1. Open a tour → Add Panorama → From Phone.
  2. Select one equirectangular image.
  3. Expected: Panorama is added, thumbnail shows in the list, count increases by 1.

TC-2 — Add multiple panoramas

  1. Select several images at once (if multi-select supported).
  2. Expected: All are imported and listed in order.

TC-3 — Permission denied

  1. Deny photo-library permission, then try to add.
  2. Expected: Clear message guiding the user to enable permission; no crash.

TC-4 — Persistence after restart

  1. Add a panorama, force-close and relaunch, reopen the tour.
  2. Expected: Panorama and its image file persist.

TC-5 — Offline import

  1. Go offline and add a panorama.
  2. Expected: Import succeeds locally with no network error.

TC-6 — Invalid / non-image file

  1. Attempt to pick an unsupported file (if reachable).
  2. Expected: Graceful rejection with a message; no broken entry created.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: existing panorama list rendering unaffected.

[Tour Detail] Integrate Delete Panorama (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: panoramas and connections data model (docs/analyze.md §3.3). Deleting a panorama must also clean up its connections and local files.

Goal

Implement "Delete Panorama" in Tour Detail: remove a selected panorama, its related connections, and its local image files, with a confirmation step.

Scope

  • Delete action on a panorama (with confirm dialog).
  • Remove the panoramas row, any connections where it is main_id or link_id, and delete its local image files (original/thumbnail/small/tiny).
  • Update the Tour Detail list and any counts immediately.

Out of Scope

  • Bulk delete; undo/restore; server-side deletion of already-uploaded panoramas.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Deleting a panorama prompts for confirmation.
  • On confirm: panoramas row removed, related connections removed, local files deleted.
  • List/counts update immediately without restart.
  • Cancel leaves everything unchanged.
  • Works offline; no orphaned connections or files remain.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Delete a panorama (happy path)

  1. Open a tour with several panoramas → delete one → confirm.
  2. Expected: Panorama disappears from the list; count decreases by 1.

TC-2 — Connections cleaned up

  1. Delete a panorama that is connected to others.
  2. Expected: Its connections are removed; remaining panoramas show no broken links.

TC-3 — Cancel delete

  1. Tap delete, then cancel on the confirm dialog.
  2. Expected: Nothing is deleted.

TC-4 — Local files removed

  1. Delete a panorama and inspect the Panorama folder.
  2. Expected: Its image files (original/thumbnail/small/tiny) are gone — no leftover files.

TC-5 — Persistence after restart

  1. Delete a panorama, relaunch, reopen the tour.
  2. Expected: It stays deleted; no reappearance.

TC-6 — Delete last panorama

  1. Delete the only panorama in a tour.
  2. Expected: Empty state shown; no crash; tour still valid.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: deleting one panorama does not affect unrelated panoramas/levels.
